## Summary

I implemented the requirement: **creating an owner whose normalized telephone already belongs to another owner is now rejected with HTTP 409 Conflict.**

### Change
`src/main/java/.../rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java` — in `addOwner`, after normalizing the incoming telephone to 10 digits (existing logic), I added a check that scans existing owners and returns `409 CONFLICT` if any of them has a telephone that normalizes to the same digits:

```java
boolean telephoneInUse = this.clinicService.findAllOwners().stream()
    .map(Owner::getTelephone)
    .filter(existing -> existing != null)
    .map(existing -> existing.replaceAll("\\D", ""))
    .anyMatch(telephone::equals);
if (telephoneInUse) {
    return new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.CONFLICT);
}
```

Comparison is done on the normalized (digits-only) form on both sides, so differently-formatted numbers that represent the same telephone are treated as duplicates.

### Test changes
`OwnerRestControllerV1Tests.java`:
- **`createOwnerDuplicateTelephoneReturnsConflict`** (new) — seeds an owner with `6081234567`, then POSTs a new owner with `(608) 123-4567`, asserting `409` (also verifies normalization matching).
- **`createOwnerSuccess`** (updated) — its telephone `6085551023` collided with the seeded George Franklin owner in the H2 fixture data, which is exactly the duplicate case the spec now rejects. I changed it to a telephone (`9995551234`) not present in the seed data, so it still verifies successful creation. This was a necessary consequence of the new behavior, not a change to what the test asserts.

Everything else was left untouched, and the change follows the existing controller's normalization idiom. The v2 controller has no create endpoint, so no change was needed there.
